name: Zipfelsalpe
kurzbeschreibung: Zipfelsalpe in Tirol Discover the breathtaking Zipfelsalpe in the heart of Tirol, where untouched alpine beauty meets endless adventure.
beschreibung:
Overview

The "Zipfelsalpe" entry refers to a hiking destination in the border area between the Tyrolean Tannheimer Tal and the Allgäu. The Tannheimer Tal lies in the district of Reutte (Ausserfern region) and is one of the best-known high valleys in the Alps. A definitive confirmation as a Tyrolean catering establishment was not possible based on the available sources: the coordinates given in the entry (47.4919 / 10.4258) mark a point south of the national border, while the hike described in the sources starts from Schattwald on the Tyrolean side. The entry is therefore not substantiated as a Tyrolean establishment.

History/Background

In the sources, the Tannheimer Tal is described as "probably the most beautiful high valley in Europe" and forms a cross-border natural area with the neighbouring Allgäu. The documented circular hike leads from Schattwald through the Stuibental, past the Wannenjoch, into the Ostrachtal. Along the way lies the ruin of the Oberer Stuiben, which points to the long tradition of alpine farming and pasture management at this altitude. The route connects Tyrolean and Allgäu alpine pastures and is designated as a circular tour with an option to stop for refreshments.

Getting there

According to the source, arrival is from the north via the A7 motorway, exit "Oy-Mittelberg", continuing on the B310 via Wertach to Oberjoch and following the "Tannheimer Tal" signs on the B199, exit Schattwald in the direction of the Wannenjoch-Bergbahn. From the Tyrolean side, the route leads via Reutte on the B198 towards the Lechtal to Weißenbach and over the Gaichtpass on the B199 to Schattwald. By public transport, one travels by train to Sonthofen, Pfronten/Ried or Reutte and then by bus to Schattwald. Parking is available at the valley station of the Wannenjochbahn in Schattwald; parking is subject to a fee. The starting and finishing point of the described tour is in each case the lift car park in Schattwald.

Tips

For the described circular tour, the 3-seater chairlift to the Wannenjoch mountain station can be used for the ascent or descent; from the mountain station an easy ascent and descent leads to the destination. As an option to stop for refreshments, the sources mention among others the "Stube 15.60" at the mountain station. The tour is described as family-friendly, with great views and interesting from a botanical and geological point of view; it runs along gravel paths with around 747 metres of elevation gain, takes about three hours according to the source, and should only be undertaken in safe weather. The weather in the mountains can change quickly, so stay on marked paths and check your personal equipment.

Best time to travel

May to October are given as the most favourable seasons. During this period the summer mountain lifts are in operation and the paths are generally passable. In spring and autumn, changes in the weather and remaining snow are to be expected at higher elevations. Before the tour, it is advisable to check the current weather and facility information for the Tannheimer Tal.
